Counsel for Applicant :- Aakash Srivastava,Apoorv Srivastava Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA and perused the record.

2. The accused-applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.542 of 2023 under sections 504, 506, 354,
376-D IPC and section 9-m/10 POCSO Act, P.S. Pihani, District Hardoi.
3. In terms of the FIR, it was alleged that on 19.09.2023 when the informant was returning along with her daughter aged about 10 years, three persons named in the FIR misbehaved with them.
The applicant was not named in the FIR.

Subsequently, in the statement under section 161 Cr.P.C., the statement was made against the applicant and three other persons alleging the commission of the Noor Ali @ Munna vs State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Deptt. Of Home ... on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156582478/
1 offence under section 376 IPC.

entities.text: Noor Ali @ Munna vs State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Deptt. Of Home
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the statement under section 164 Cr.P.C., the statement made under section 161 Cr.P.C. was reiterated.
4. The counsel for the applicant argues that no allegation of offence under section 376 IPC was levelled in the FIR whereas the informant is aged about 35 years.
Thus, the entire case is false.
He argues that the allegations of rape by four persons do not support the medical evidence on record.

He further argues that the applicant had got registered a first information report against the informant being FIR No.0568 of 2022 and as a sequence of the said FIR, the applicant has been roped in only through the statements under sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
5.
Considering the said submissions, prima-facie the applicant was not even named in the FIR and his name surfaced only in the statement under sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.

The allegations specially the gravity of the offence alleged is clearly not supported by the medical on record coupled with the fact that the applicant had also lodged an FIR against the informant, as such, on all these considerations, a case for bail is made out particularly insofar as the daughter of the informant is concerned, the allegation of offence are under sections 9-m/10 of the POCSO Act and the fact that the applicant has no criminal history and is in jail since 02.10.2023.
Thus the bail application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant Noor Ali @ Munna be released on bail in aforesaid first information report number subject to his furnishing a personal bond and two reliable sureties of Rs.25000/- (Twenty Five Thousand) each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 16.1.2024 VNP/-
